children: For investors staring at the calendar after Oct. 14, history has usually offered a fairly encouraging answer.
Data going back more than seven decades show that
all 11 major S&P 500 sectors have historically posted positive returns in most years from the Oct. 14 close through year-end
, with win rates ranging from roughly 70% to 82%.
Healthcare has been the standout.
The sector has gained
5.7% on average
over the period while finishing higher
81% of the time
. Its median return was even stronger at 6.8%, suggesting the result has not depended entirely on a handful of unusually strong years.
That gives investors something more useful than a simple stocks usually rise into year-end argument.
The strength has been broad.
Consumer discretionary has averaged a
3.4% gain
, while energy has returned about
, with both sectors finishing higher in roughly seven out of every 10 periods studied.
Technology, industrials and materials have produced average gains in the
mid-to-high 4% range
, while utilities and consumer staples have historically delivered smaller but steadier advances.
The pattern is broad, but not equally smooth
The seasonal tailwind does not mean every sector has behaved the same way.
Technology has produced some of the strongest gains, but also the widest swings. Consumer staples, by contrast, have shown much lower volatility.
That difference matters.
An investor chasing the highest historical average return may be accepting considerably more risk than someone favoring defensive sectors with narrower ranges of outcomes.
The common thread is timing.
Mid-October has historically fallen near the point when U.S. equities begin one of their stronger seasonal stretches, with performance often improving as the market moves toward year-end.

title: S&P 500 Sectors Enter Powerful Historical Stretch
